sermon.title: The Season of Salvation
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this first session on present truth, Pastor David G. Kincer says God works in seasons and that the present season, the last days before Christ’s return, is a season of salvation. He separates present truth from future events no one can date, and walks through signs he says are already fulfilled or under way: antichrists and persecution, the falling away, restoration, the gospel to all nations, increased knowledge and Israel becoming a nation.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: This is presented as the first session on “present truth.” At 13:15 he cites “Luke 21 11” and then quotes the next verse on persecution (Luke 21:12). Names of movements and people are spelled as heard; where a name was not clear it is marked [unclear]. Historical dates and figures (e.g. 313 A.D., 476 A.D., 1517, the revival years, 2600 years, the share of non-religious Israelis) are given as spoken and have not been checked.

He says to expect Christianity to keep growing in all nations and a glorious church without spot or wrinkle before Christ returns.

faqs.question: How can you be at peace in bad seasons?
faqs.answer: He says if you know the seasons of God you are at peace, even in what others call bad seasons, because you understand God has a purpose during that season.

faqs.question: Should we trust people who predict the date of Jesus’ return?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus plainly said nobody knows but God himself, yet people keep prophesying and predicting dates about future things that are not present truth.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a false prophet and an antichrist?
faqs.answer: He says the antichrist does not believe Jesus is the Messiah, God in the flesh, while false prophets believe but teach things that lead you away from him.

faqs.question: How long was the early church persecuted?
faqs.answer: He says the early church was heavily persecuted up to 313 A.D.

faqs.question: Why couldn’t people read the Bible in the dark ages?
faqs.answer: He says the Bible was written by hand, poor people could not afford one, and they were forbidden to read it because only the priests could tell them what it said.

faqs.question: Can someone who fell away be restored?
faqs.answer: He says we are living in the season of restoration and awakening; if you fell back you can be restored, and if you are dry or dead you can be refreshed and renewed.

faqs.question: What should be preached to the nations?
faqs.answer: He says not psychiatry, psychology, possibility thinking or purpose driven thinking, but the gospel with a witness: repentance and remission of sins in Jesus’ name.

scriptures.text_nkjv: and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in His name to all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.

faqs.question: What is the danger of increased knowledge?
faqs.answer: He says people think they can get saved and grow in God with just knowledge and not the spirit of the word and the Spirit of God that gives life to that knowledge.

faqs.question: Where does he say Christianity is growing?
faqs.answer: He says to expect Christianity to keep growing in South America, Africa and Asia, with millions coming to Christ every year, while Europe and America are getting cold.
